correctness.rationale: The frozen Finding's description of the exponent as noninteger across the stated domain is not valid: α=d=1 and q=1/3 obey the hypotheses and yield ν=1. The complete repaired RESULT.md distinguishes a power that need not be an integer from an assertion that it never is; it also clarifies that the exceptional curve has no power-law factor. The exact formulas and all parameter hypotheses are unchanged. In physical time the ratio change gives u'=u(λ−u), z'=z(h+u). At the fold h=h'=0 and h''=−α²(d+1), so the coefficient of w² in z' is −κ, while λ(z*)=−μ and λ'(z*)=−α(d+1)q. A small rectangle above z* has inward top and bottom edges and u≤u(0)e^(−μt/2). For any fixed η>0 the angular drift is eventually uniformly negative on z≥z*+η inside it, proving z→z*. The inequality w'≥−Mw² gives w≥1/(w(0)^(−1)+Mt), so the forcing (z*+w)u/w² in (1/w)' is integrable. Integrating (1/w)'=κ+O(w)−(z*+w)u/w² first gives 1/w∼κt and then 1/w=κt+O(log t). The difference w−1/(κt), as well as w² and u, is integrable on the late-time interval; integrating (log u)' therefore gives the positive finite normalized amplitude and exponent −λ'(z*)/κ. The isolated stable eigenvalue −μ yields a smooth local strong-stable graph tangent to (1,−z*/μ); along its positive branch the radial correction is O(u) and integrable, giving the pure exponential limit. At (1,0) the eigenvalues are −1 and b−d, so b<d separately gives an open positive-data prey-only basin. The verification script was inspected but not run; its finite diagnostic is not used as proof.

value.rationale: At a previously motivated boundary of attraction, the theorem resolves two observable scales and the distinction between an open extinction sector and an exceptional curve. It gives a quantitative model benchmark unavailable from eigenvalues and proves coexistence of open basins at the threshold when b<d. The value is the correction and exact asymptotics, not a universal claim of nonintegrality or a global basin classification.
